subject: EverGrove commercial terms - exec authorization request for contract redlines
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@evergrovehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@evergrovehealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract redlines - liability and indemnity concerns
Attachments: EverGrove_Redlines_EVGSOW_v3.pdf

Ben —

Thanks again for a productive week. Attached are the redlines from our GC team (SOW + commercial terms). The main items blocking procurement are:

- Removal of liability cap for data incidents (our GC wants unlimited recovery for certain data harms).
- Broad indemnity for IP claims that would make EverGrove responsible for third-party claims tied to our customers.
- Warranty language expanded to a 12-month uptime/availability warranty (we asked for narrower language).

This opportunity is significant for us but Procurement needs clarity on what Redwood is willing to accept. Can you confirm Redwood's position on: 

1) Liability cap for incidents involving customer data
2) Whether you can accept a mutual IP indemnity or limit IP indemnity to willful infringement
3) Warranty term and remedies (we'd like explicit credits / termination rights tied to uptime)

We'd like to get to a final SOW by early next week. Please let me know if this requires escalation on your side.

—Elena Ruiz
SVP, Procurement
EverGrove Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Contract redlines - liability and indemnity concerns
Attachments: EVG_Redline_Summary.xlsx

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding EverGrove's redlines (attached summary). Quick context: EVG is a mid-market health tech chain, $1.2M ARR expected first-year consumption for our hosted API + dedicated pilot. Procurement has pushed aggressive asks to close the deal before their next quarter.

Key asks from EVG:
- Remove or materially raise liability cap (they want no cap for certain data incidents)
- Broad indemnity for IP and third-party claims
- Expanded warranty with explicit uptime credits and potential termination rights

My proposed commercial trade-offs to keep the deal:
Option A (lower risk, slower close): hold standard $250k cap, insist on mutual IP indemnity limited to willful misconduct, 6-month warranty, no additional credit beyond standard SLA credits.
Option B (accelerate close): one-time exec exception to increase cap to $500k, accept mutual IP indemnity with carveouts, allow a 6-month warranty and define SLA credits; offer a 12% one-time discount as concession.

Ask: Legal needs exec authorization to accept anything above $250k cap or to change our standard indemnity posture. Lauren — can you sign off on Option B (one-time exception) if Legal confirms language, or do you want to stick with Option A? If we don't move, risk losing the deal.

Thanks — I can take the final DocuSign once we have approval.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract redlines - liability and indemnity concerns

Thanks Ben — reviewed EVG's redlines and flagged required approvals. Summary of legal position: 

- Liability cap: Our standard SOW cap is $250,000. We can accept an increase to $500,000 for strategic deals, but anything beyond $500,000 requires GC + CEO sign-off. If we raise the cap we should: (a) narrow the scope to direct damages only, (b) carve out claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (c) exclude consequential damages explicitly.

- IP indemnity: We do not accept unilateral broad IP indemnities. Legal will accept a mutual IP indemnity limited to: (a) third-party infringement claims caused by that party's negligence or willful infringement; (b) caps aligned with the commercial cap; and (c) notice and control requirements for defense. Removing reciprocal indemnity is a non-starter without C-suite approval.

- Warranty: We recommend limiting express warranties to 6 months from delivery and defining SLA credits (tiered credits for uptime < 99.5%, 99.0% thresholds). We can offer termination rights only for repeated, uncured SLA breaches (not single incidents).

Commercial ask: if Sales wants to go with Ben's Option B (one-time exception to $500k plus 12% discount), Legal will draft redline language that implements the cap carve-outs and mutual IP language, but we need Lauren's explicit authorization for the $500k exception and the discount. Also request DealDesk ticket and HubSpot update with the negotiated concessions.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Risk
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Contract redlines - liability and indemnity concerns

Thanks for the clear framing. I authorize a one-time exception under the following conditions: 

- Liability cap increased to $500,000 (applies to direct damages only).
- Cap explicitly excludes consequential damages and is subject to carve-outs for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- Accept mutual IP indemnity limited to willful infringement/negligence and capped at the commercial liability cap.
- Warranty term limited to 6 months; SLA credits to be defined by Legal per Marissa's tiers (no unilateral termination for single incidents).
- Commercial concession: approve a one-time 10% credit applied to the first invoice (not a change to list price going forward).

Marissa — proceed to draft final redlines implementing the above and include precise SLA language. Ben — proceed to update HubSpot (EVG-2027-114) with the negotiated concessions and route the DocuSign package once Legal uploads the final. Close timeline: we expect signed SOW no later than EOD Monday, 6/14.

If any counter from EVG materially changes the ask (e.g., asks for >$500k cap or permanent pricing change), escalate to me and CC the CFO.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop | Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
